full_judgment:
Shahidul Karim J: On an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in brief, the Code), Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the accused-petitioner should not be enlarged on bail in Gulshan Police Station Case No.59 dated 23-9-2015 under sections 409/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 now pending in the Court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The case is still under investigation and no investigation report has yet been submitted against any of the accused. 

 4. The petitioner was arrested on 7-1-2016  who thereupon unsuccessful moved application for bail before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and thereafter, filed a Criminal Miscellaneous Case being No. 6309 of 2016 before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka which was also turned down by order dated 7-9-2016. Being aggrieved thereby, the accused-petitioner moved this Court and obtained the instant Rule. 

 5. Mr Pankaj Kumar Kundu, learned Advocate along with Mr Mohiuddin Ahmed appearing for the accused-petitioner submits that the accused-petitioner Sipar Ahmed is completely innocent who has been implicated in the case as he was the former branch manager of BASIC Bank Limited, Gulshan Branch, Dhaka. He further submits that being a bank manager the accused-petitioner was rather compelled to forward the impugned SOD loan application to the head office as per direction of the then Chairman and Managing Director of BASIC Bank Limited. Moreover, the petitioner was arrested 7-1-2016 and the investigation of the case has not yet been completed despite expiry of the statutory period for completion of investigation. Lastly, the learned Advocate submits that in a similar case FIR named co-accused No.5 Fozlus Sobhan has already been enlarged on bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 16306 of 2016 against which the Durnity Daman Commission unsuccessfully moved a Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal being No.939 of 2016. 

 7. Heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties and perused the application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure including the supplementary affidavit dated 3-8-2017 and also considered the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 8. Having gone through the materials on record it appears that the accused-petitioner was the former manager of BASIC Bank Limited, Gulshan Branch, Dhaka who in his official capacity forwarded the impugned SOD loan application of FIR named accused No. 1 Mohiuddin Sheikh to the head office of the bank. Admittedly, the accused-petitioner has got no authority to approve the credit facility of any intended client. In the instant case the accused-petitioner disbursed the loan amount after the SOD loan application was approved by the board of the directors of the concerned bank. Materials on record further reveal that the case was lodged on 23-9-2015 and the accused-petitioner was nabbed on 7-1-2016, but till today the investigation authority has failed to complete the investigation of the case. It also appears that in a similar category of case the FIR named accused No.5 Fazlus Sobhan has already been admitted to bail by another bench of this Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 16306 of 2016 against which the Anti-Corruption Commission moved a Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 939 of 2016 before the Appellate Division which was eventually dismissed meaning thereby that the bail order of the said accused has been maintained. 

 10. In this context, we would like to dwell upon another issue centering round the instant loan scam. It appears that during enquiry/ investigation of the instant case the accused-petitioner submitted a written statement before the team leader of the enquiry committee formed by the ACC. We feel tempted to quote the said statement of the accused-petitioner in verbatim which was filed by way of supplementary affidavit dated 3-8-2017, which runs as underneath: 

 14. The accused-petitioner Sipar Ahmed is allowed to go on bail in Gulshan Police Station Case No. 59(9)2015 corresponding to ACC GR Case No.626 of 2015 under sections 409/ 467/ 468/471/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 on furnishing bail bond to the satisfaction of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka.
